primitives.name: Hierarchical Ability Blending
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Equations / assumptions - Team ability = E_continent + E_country + E_league + E_team (Elo components), rescaled 0–100 daily.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_{\\text{team}}': 'Team ability score (0–100)', 'E_{\\text{continent}}': 'Continent Elo component (dimensionless)', 'E_{\\text{country}}': 'Country Elo component (dimensionless)', 'E_{\\text{league}}': 'League Elo component (dimensionless)', 'E_{\\text{team}}': 'Team Elo component (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Elo components are additive and rescaled to 0–100; team ability is static during a transfer period.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When team or league data is insufficient, fallback to higher hierarchy levels.

primitives.name: Feature Blend Equation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Assumptions: event data consistent across leagues; position labels from formations are adequate role proxies (authors flag moving to learned "Player Roles" as future work); 1,000-minute horizon; no defensive "opposition allowed" metrics or goalkeeping yet (future work: xGoT, Ramos-at-PSG-style defensive impact).
primitives.latex: X'_{i,j,g} = (1 - w_{j,g}) P_{i,j} + w_{j,g} R_{i,j,g}, \quad w_{j,g} = \min(1, \frac{\sum \text{minutes}}{c})
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {"X'_{i,j,g}": 'Blended feature vector for player i at team j in position g', 'P_{i,j}': 'Prior feature estimate for player i at team j', 'R_{i,j,g}': 'Recent feature estimate for player i at team j in position g', 'w_{j,g}': 'Blend weight (0–1)', 'c': 'Prior→data blend constant (1000)', '\\sum \\text{minutes}': 'Total minutes played in new environment'}
primitives.assumptions: Prior estimates are valid for low-data cases; blend weight increases with observed minutes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When minutes < c, weight < 1; when minutes ≥ c, weight = 1.

layer2.mapping: GSE's feature pipeline uses this to dynamically adjust player stats based on limited game exposure post-transfer.
layer2.telemetry: Observed vs. predicted per-90 metrics after 1000-minute horizon.

primitives.name: Shortlist Scoring
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Shortlist score: Σ_k (weight_k × normalized predicted metric_k) / Σ_k weight_k, weights ∈ [0,1] user-set.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{Score}': 'Normalized shortlist score (dimensionless)', 'w_k': 'User-defined weight for metric k (0–1)', '\\text{norm}_k': 'Normalized predicted metric k (0–1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Weights are user-defined and sum to positive value; metrics are normalized before aggregation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When all weights are zero, score is undefined; when weights vary, score reflects relative importance.

layer2.mapping: GSI's recommendation engine uses this to rank potential transfers based on weighted performance forecasts.
layer2.telemetry: Ranking consistency between predicted and actual performance of top-ranked players.

Each module contributes distinct but interlinked elements: (1) Hierarchical ability blending provides a robust baseline for team strength, which is essential for contextualizing player performance. (2) The feature blend equation allows for adaptive updating of player stats based on observed minutes, addressing data scarcity in early stages post-transfer. (3) Shortlist scoring aggregates these predictions into actionable recommendations. These primitives form a dual system: one for forecasting (NNs) and one for ranking (scoring). Failure modes include overfitting in small sample sizes, misalignment of position proxies, and lack of defensive metrics. The system assumes consistent event data and static team ability during a transfer window, which may break down in volatile environments.
